about: Concept IDs, retired IDs and the checks of review and of run of the Ontology as Specification approach, generated by gen-approach.mjs from its ontology, catalogue and run guide. Copy it with the tool.

checks.given: a term is renamed
checks.then: the ID is the same and only the row's text changed

checks.given: a note under a definition table
checks.then: it adds detail and does not restate the definition

checks.given: a new definition row
checks.then: it says what the thing is in a sentence or two, not how it is stored

checks.given: a rule, invariant or action that involves several entities
checks.then: it sits with the entity it constrains or changes

checks.given: a new definition row
checks.then: it defines a kind of thing, its field, its relation or a rule, not one particular object, person or moment

checks.given: a definition row whose definition changed
checks.when: a reviewer compares it with the base
checks.then: if the ID now names another thing, the old ID is retired with its replacement and a decision; if the row describes the same thing better, the ID stays

checks.given: a link added by a change, a `ref` or `refs` type or a view's `shows`
checks.when: a reviewer reads it with the rows it joins
checks.then: it names a relation that holds in the product, and no entity exists only to join others

checks.given: a slice of code, the mockup included
checks.when: a reviewer compares it with the ontology
checks.then: everything it does is stated by a definition row or a check; what is not becomes a check or a question before the slice is done

checks.given: a view or an action
checks.when: a reviewer reads its rows and its checks
checks.then: what the view shows in each state, what the user can do there and every outcome of the action are stated; layout and style are not asked for

checks.given: a change that alters what the product does
checks.then: the ontology's rows or checks change in the same change or before the code

checks.given: a new entry
checks.then: it answers one question; a part that answers another question is its own entry

checks.given: a new entry that touches something an earlier entry decided
checks.then: the new entry only adds and the earlier one stays in force, or it supersedes the earlier one whole on its `Supersedes:` line

checks.given: a rule in the ontology that looks arbitrary without its reason
checks.then: it names the decision by number

checks.given: a new entry
checks.then: it is a choice someone working on the product needs to know

checks.given: an entry whose value an agent picked after being asked to tune the model
checks.then: the entry is tentative until the owner accepts it

checks.given: a change of the default values of a model
checks.then: it is a short entry about the topic of the values, tentative when an agent chose them; a setting tuned toward a requirement has no entry

checks.given: a new entry
checks.then: it says why, and lists the rejected alternatives with their reasons

checks.given: an entry that replaces an earlier one
checks.then: it names the entries it supersedes

checks.given: a change to the ontology that rests on a choice
checks.then: a decision entry records the choice

checks.given: the owner's message and an answer a colleague gave for the owner disagree about one choice
checks.then: it follows the owner's message and names it on its `Source:` line; an entry resting only on the colleague's answer is tentative

checks.given: an entry whose source is a statement of an author who is not certain
checks.then: it is tentative, and it does not call the statement the owner's

checks.given: a question with options and a recommendation
checks.then: it is a tentative entry whose decision is the recommendation and whose rejected alternatives are the other options, not a line under open questions

checks.given: a tentative entry or an open question waits for the owner
checks.then: it asks what no run can settle; a question about speed, fit or behavior carries the result of a prototype instead of waiting

checks.given: the owner answers a tentative entry
checks.then: the entry is accepted as written or as rewritten to the chosen option and names the answer on its `Source:` line, and History records the acceptance; the entry of a dropped question is removed, and History says so

checks.given: something is put off: a target concept or an item out of scope
checks.then: an entry defers it with a `Return when:` line

checks.given: a change to behavior
checks.then: the implementation table changed in the same change, and the note of a partial row names the target concept that adds what is missing

checks.given: a row of the implementation table
checks.when: a reviewer opens the files it names
checks.then: they realise the concept

checks.given: code that implements a concept
checks.then: an `ont:` comment next to the code names the concept

checks.given: a blind walk found that renewal goes through while someone waits, that the hold queue is not served, and that nothing says what a damaged item shows
checks.then: the walker had no access to the code; the renewal became a known divergence, the case of the damaged item a check, and the queue nothing new, since it is target

checks.given: a new line under known divergences
checks.then: it describes behavior that contradicts the target, not something missing

checks.given: a known divergence
checks.then: it points at a ticket or a pending decision, and neither side was edited to hide it

checks.given: the mockup
checks.when: an agent opens it from the file system, by the approach's run guide
checks.then: there is one mockup for the product, it runs without a build, and it shows the target

checks.given: a mockup shared outside the team
checks.then: it holds no real names or records

checks.given: an element labelled with an action
checks.when: an agent uses it in the mockup, by the approach's run guide
checks.then: it does what the action's definition says

checks.given: the map
checks.then: it is grouped by screen with one row per element

checks.given: an element the mockup deliberately leaves without some behavior, such as a button that is never offered
checks.when: a reviewer looks for the reason
checks.then: the ontology states it, in a definition, a note of the screen or the out-of-scope list, and the map does not

checks.given: a new check
checks.then: it names members, items and dates from the sample, and no function, command or selector

checks.given: a check of review or run that could not be carried out
checks.then: it says not run, and the evidence of the checks that ran is kept by check and date

checks.given: a decision that chooses a value, a requirement or the assumptions of a model
checks.then: an automatic check holds the value or the requirement; for the model, a check holds a snapshot of its base scenario's results, and none requires it to reach its goal

checks.given: a judged check of a summary the product writes
checks.then: the judge gets the check's case and the summary, and neither the code nor an expected text

checks.given: a judged check that ran
checks.then: its verdict is kept outside the repository, named by the check and the date

checks.given: an implemented view whose note describes its states
checks.when: a reviewer compares the note with the catalogue
checks.then: every state the note describes has a judged check whose THEN says what the note says for it

checks.given: a run of a view's judged checks
checks.when: a reviewer looks for its screens
checks.then: they are outside the repository, named by view, state and date, and the owner can open them

checks.given: two checks of `action.renew` whose cases differ only in the member and the title
checks.then: one of them goes

checks.given: a case the catalogue does not hold, with the owner's answer kept outside the catalogue
checks.when: a fresh reader, a model without context that sees only the ontology and the catalogue, says what should happen
checks.then: it matches the owner's answer; a mismatch adds a check, or an open question when the owner does not know the answer

checks.given: a review of a change in a project that sets `verdicts`
checks.when: a reviewer looks for its records
checks.then: every verdict of the review has a record, and each record that needs evidence links to it outside the repository

checks.given: a finding of a round of review
checks.then: the report says where else the same class of problem was looked for

checks.given: with `mergeGate.taskState` and `mergeGate.verdicts` at the base, a change of a task whose last round of the review of the result is clean; one after the narrow round that follows a confirmed condition with the record of done that ends the range of fixes; one whose last round has a finding; and one whose step ended clean with a failed verdict of the record of a round in its window
checks.when: the guard reads the records at the head
checks.then: it passes the first two and refuses the third, `TASK_NOT_DONE`, and the fourth, `VERDICT_FAILED`: readiness is computed from the records, not given by a verdict that would depend on itself

checks.given: a round that follows stagnation, with the analysis of the cause its brief carried
checks.when: a reviewer reads the analysis, its rounds and the change
checks.then: the analysis names the cause, for a repeated class why the earlier fix did not hold and the one cause behind it, for no fewer findings why the round found no fewer; what was chosen follows from it: the design changed where the cause lies in it, the error fixed otherwise, a rare case filed (`rule.findings-filed`); the reviewer writes a finding when the cause is not named or the choice does not follow from it; and the round was the one `derived.next-round` names: full, or, after a round C of the condition confirmed that stagnated, the one narrow round

checks.given: a finding filed as `limitation` or `later`, and a finding kept fixable
checks.when: the reviewer of the next round, if there is one, reads the finding, its file and the step of usual work the notes name for it
checks.then: what the approach does not do by choice is in the limitations, a fault of the tool or a finding outside the approved statement in a ticket, a finding marked usual path names the step of usual work it breaks, and no item of the approved statement is filed

checks.given: a change reviewed in a project that sets `reviewRounds`
checks.then: every round of its review has a record, with the tokens that are known and every finding

checks.given: a verdict of acceptance
checks.when: a reviewer reads it with the statement
checks.then: it answers every item of what to do and of done when, and the owner's sources, of the approved version

checks.given: a merge of a task through GitHub
checks.when: a reviewer reads the record of the merge
checks.then: it was a merge commit made through the API on the condition of the head's commit, after the head was confirmed past the reviewed commit, or, after the narrow round that follows a confirmed condition, the commit of the record of done that ends the range of fixes (`rule.fixes-held-by-tests`), by records alone

checks.given: a tagged test
checks.when: a reviewer reads it with its check
checks.then: it sets up GIVEN, does WHEN and asserts THEN

checks.given: a test of a check that a validator holds
checks.when: a reviewer reads it with its check
checks.then: it runs the validator on an input that passes and on one broken in that check's way, and asserts that check's error

checks.given: a ticket
checks.then: it lists concepts and checks; any behavior it needs is already in the catalogue

checks.given: an agent looks for work
checks.then: the slice holds ready targets only, cut into a ticket from `--next`; a target that waits for the owner is left until the owner answers

checks.given: the tickets open in a project
checks.then: each is being worked on now; none was cut ahead to hold concepts for later, and an agent that cut one did only what the owner allows

checks.given: a ticket whose `--gap` prints `SLICE_DONE` and whose tests pass
checks.then: it is closed, and its file or its tracker entry is still there

checks.given: several agents start work at the same time, each on a branch of its own
checks.when: a reviewer reads the tickets they work from
checks.then: one coordinator cut them all, they were on the main branch before the agents started, and no concept is in two of them

checks.given: a ticket cut from what `--next` proposed
checks.when: a reviewer reads the change that closes it
checks.then: it is one change the reviewer can follow with its tests; if not, the ticket should have been split along the dependencies, the part the rest depends on first

checks.given: the agent rules section
checks.then: it fits on one screen and every row names a path or a command

checks.given: a task for an agent
checks.then: it names the IDs the task touches before writing code

checks.given: a consistency review of a project
checks.then: each one says who would be misled or which check would break; style, list completeness and compliance that changes nothing are left out

checks.given: an agent accepted a decision entry as part of a change
checks.then: the change is in a commit of its own files and no one else's, so the guard protects the entry; whether the commit or a push waited for an approval is the user's choice

checks.given: a change to a rule of the approach
checks.then: the reviewer did not write it and got the diff and the IDs it touches, not the author's conclusions

checks.given: a process rule in the agent instructions, such as one that says agents do not commit
checks.then: it names the rule of the approach or the entry it comes from, and a rule that departs from the approach cites a process entry that extends or overrides it. The tool cannot tell a process rule from a command or a matter of style, nor whether a rule written in prose is stricter or looser than the approach

checks.given: an agent was corrected for a mistake it could make again
checks.when: a reviewer reads the change that holds the correction
checks.then: it is held by the structure of the code, a check, a test or a lint where one of them can hold it; a rule in the agent instructions only where none can, and the rule says so

checks.given: with `mergeGate.verdicts` at the base, a change of a task whose records give a verdict to each check of the list of the change, with a not-run with its reason; one with a check of the list without one; one whose latest record of a check is a fail of a class not decided; and one whose check of errors in code was given on a commit of records alone
checks.when: the guard reads the records at the head
checks.then: it passes the first and refuses the others, `VERDICT_MISSING`, `VERDICT_FAILED` and `VERDICT_NOT_OF_CHANGE`: that the change was reviewed is computed from the records, not given by a verdict that would depend on itself

checks.given: a change that adds or alters a value with a source
checks.then: the reviewer opened the source of each such value, gave the project's check of values against their source a verdict, and recorded it; a source it could not open is not-run with the reason

checks.given: a change that touches code
checks.when: its reviewer reads the diff, after the narrow round that follows a confirmed condition the diff of the fixes, once (`rule.fixes-held-by-tests`)
checks.then: the change brings no error of correctness and no security problem: no secret in the code, no unchecked input that reaches a query, a command or a path, no access wider than the change needs, no dependency with a known flaw; each one found is reported with its file and line

checks.given: a page of a doc set
checks.then: each anchor names what its section is about, an empty one stands only above a section that explains no concept, and no section copies a definition

checks.given: sections listed to reread
checks.then: they reread each section first and fixed what changed

checks.given: a section of a run guide
checks.when: a fresh reader who has not seen the product, a model without context given only the section, follows it
checks.then: they run the check, and the section names the check without restating its case

checks.given: a change of the tree or of the page that explains it
checks.then: the rows under an entity are shown and described as the rows of its table, never as kinds or parts of it, and the page shows nothing beyond the structure but its footer, which says what it was built from: the commit, the configuration and the date

checks.given: a merge of a task through GitHub
checks.when: a reviewer reads the executor's report of the merge
checks.then: it says the clone that serves the tree was brought to the merge commit and the page names that commit

checks.given: a profile
checks.then: everything it requires is enforced through the configuration and the catalogue, and the rest is listed as recommended

checks.given: a release about to be trusted
checks.when: its reviewer runs `--verify` on it, by the approach's run guide
checks.then: `--verify` passes on it

checks.given: a change that adds or changes formal forms
checks.then: nothing runs the oracle as the product, and the code is still written by a model from the ontology

checks.given: a project with an oracle and code
checks.when: a reviewer reads its comparison test
checks.then: it runs the code and the oracle on the same random sequences of implemented actions, fails on a difference that is not a known divergence with its condition, fails when nothing is compared, and keeps a failing sequence to repeat it
